Ravi P.: FYI - saw a big uptick in TLS resumption failures in ap-south ~10m after the HSM migration window. Latency spikes and many clients re-doing full ECDHE.
Hannah Q.: interesting, does full handshake succeed? or are connections dropping?
Ravi P.: full handshakes are succeeding, but resumption (ticket/psk) attempts fail with `decrypt failed: key not available` in the envoy logs. Example: `envoy tls: session ticket decrypt error: kms: failed to unwrap key: resource not found`
Theo L.: which key did we migrate? session-ticket-key-v2? That one is HSM-protected now. Might be an IAM or HSM policy problem.
Iris (oncall): grabbing keystore + HSM logs. Can someone paste the KMS audit entries for the failed unwrapping?
Ravi P.: pasted from cloud audit: 
```
logName: projects/redwood/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity
protoPayload.methodName: "cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.asymmetricDecrypt"
protoPayload.status.code: 7
protoPayload.resourceName: "projects/redwood/locations/ap-south/keyRings/kr-prod/cryptoKeys/session-ticket-key/cryptoKeyVersions/3"
protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp: "10.8.5.72"
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail: "service-account:envoy-keystore@infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
```
And later: `errorMessage: "Key not available in HSM slot"`
Hannah Q.: hm. that sounds like the key material is not yet mirrored to the HSM cluster node serving ap-south or the HSM has a cluster pin/role not granted. Could be replication lag during migration.
Theo L.: also check IAM conditions on the HSM key. We have a deny policy to prevent regional reads during migration windows. Maybe rule accidentally applied to the live key.
Iris (oncall): quick mitigation proposals: 1) revert to software-protected key version (v1) for session tickets on ap-south proxies, 2) create a temporary allow binding to the HSM cluster node SA, or 3) disable session tickets (force full handshake) while we restore KMS availability. Which is least risky?
Ravi P.: option 1 is lowest blast radius if we have v1 available and not expired. It's a config flip in the keystore mapping: `SESSION_TICKET_KEY_VERSION=v1`.
Hannah Q.: option 3 is also safe (disable session tickets) but will increase CPU. We should do canary on a subset of frontends.
Theo L.: I can push an emergency canary to disable tickets for ap-south frontends: `kubectl -n prod set env deploy/frontend-proxy --containers=envoy SESSION_TICKETS_ENABLED=false --record` then watch 5% traffic shard.
ops-bot: canary rollout started: frontend-proxy ap-south/shard-1 -> env change applied to 3 pods.
Iris (oncall): meanwhile, check HSM replication status: `gcloud kms key-versions describe ... --location=ap-south` and look at `state` and `protectionLevel`. Also `hsmNodeStatus` in our internal HSM dashboard.
Ravi P.: ran describe: key version 3 protectionLevel=HSM state=ENABLED but `rotationInfo.replicationState=IN_PROGRESS` and lastReplicaTime="2026-03-21T00:10:05Z"
Hannah Q.: that confirms replication lag. We should not have pointed proxies at v3 until replication finished. Root cause: deploy sequence allowed switch before replication complete.
Theo L.: action: 1) revert mapping to v1 for ap-south (canary) -> owner me, 2) add precondition in binder/deployer so that keyVersion state==ENABLED && replicationState==COMPLETED before traffic switch -> owner Hannah, 3) add KMS audit alert for `asymmetricDecrypt` with status != OK in any region -> owner Iris.
Iris (oncall): performing the revert now on canary. command: `kubectl -n prod set env deploy/frontend-proxy --containers=envoy SESSION_TICKET_KEY_VERSION=v1`
deploy-bot: env updated on 3 pods at 1777772340.
ops-bot: health check reports: canary pod latency back to baseline after revert. Resumption accepted for new sessions.
Ravi P.: good. Confirming client log shows `session ticket accepted` for canary clients.
Hannah Q.: follow-ups: - update deployer to check KMS replication status (add API call in release pipeline), - change runbook to include HSM replication check before key switch, - add unit/integration test mocking `replicationState=IN_PROGRESS`.
Theo L.: also proposal: make session-ticket key target fallback logic in runtime: if decrypt returns HSM-specific error, try previous software key version automatically. Reduces blast radius for future migrations.
Iris (oncall): sounds good. I'll create an incident ticket INC-2026-215 and start a short postmortem after we stabilize. Add timeline: migration start, proxy switch, replication lag, detection, canary revert.
sec-bot: alert rule created: `kms.asymmetricDecrypt.failures` -> sec-stream if >3 failures in 2m for any key in prod.
Ravi P.: owners assigned: Theo = immediate revert & runtime fallback prototype, Hannah = deployer gating PR, Iris = incident doc and alerts, Theo/Hannah pair to add tests.
Hannah Q.: one more compliance note: record the HSM migration approval and window; compliance will want evidence we validated replication prior to live traffic. I'll ping legal/compliance.
ops-bot: full rollout rollback scheduled for 1777772460 if no further errors.
deploy-bot: revert completed to v1 on ap-south canary at 1777772395.
Iris (oncall): monitoring 30m, closing thread unless we see new alerts. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
